rationale: Both original blocking findings are resolved with clear fix-up evidence: CR-001 added an explicit `return` after printProxyError in the connectTargets catch (no fall-through to dispatch with unassigned state/config; tsc --noEmit and eslint clean), and CR-002 now calls printSummary unconditionally so single-target success prints the per-target 'Targets configured:' block per spec §3.4 (new unit test added; proxy suite 141/141). No new high-risk issues were introduced; business_review and standards_review carried forward from the prior round unchanged.

business_review.item: §7 connect --claude-desktop writes only Desktop config; no VS Code files touched
business_review.notes: connectTargets dispatch only pushes runClaudeDesktop when targets.claudeDesktop; runVscodeByok/runVscodeClaudeCode gated behind their own flags

business_review.item: §7 connect --vscode writes only chatLanguageModels.json
business_review.notes: only runVscodeByok runs, calling writeVsCodeLanguageModelsConfig; desktop/claude-code writers not invoked

business_review.item: §7 connect --vscode-claude-code writes only the Claude Code extension settings.json (standalone)
business_review.notes: runVscodeClaudeCode calls only writeVsCodeClaudeCodeConfig; test asserts writeDesktopConfig/writeVsCodeLanguageModelsConfig not called

business_review.item: §7 connect --claude-desktop --vscode --vscode-claude-code writes all three from one daemon lifecycle + per-target summary
business_review.notes: single ensureDaemon call, then all three run* dispatched; printSummary fires when results.length>1

business_review.item: §7 Bare connect prints friendly target list, writes nothing, starts no daemon, exits 0
business_review.notes: hasAnyTarget guard early-returns after console.log(TARGET_LIST); no config/checkStatus; exitCode untouched (0)

business_review.item: §7 --insiders with a VS Code target uses the Insiders config location
business_review.notes: insiders=Boolean(opts.insiders) threaded into writeVsCodeLanguageModelsConfig(url,insiders) and writeVsCodeClaudeCodeConfig(url,key,insiders)

business_review.item: §7 Existing config files retain unrelated keys/entries (atomic-write behavior unchanged)
business_review.notes: writers composed unchanged (out of scope); orchestrator does not alter write logic

business_review.item: §7 (negative) --claude-desktop --vscode: VS Code write fails, Desktop succeeds → Desktop stays written, failure in summary, exit non-zero
business_review.notes: per-target try/catch captures the failure; anyFailed→exitCode=1; allFailed false→no rollback so Desktop config persists; printSummary shows ✗

business_review.item: §7 (deprecation) connect desktop behaves as connect --claude-desktop and prints the notice
business_review.notes: printConnectDeprecation('desktop','--claude-desktop') then connectTargets({targets:{claudeDesktop:true}})

business_review.item: §7 (deprecation) connect vscode behaves as connect --vscode and prints the notice
business_review.notes: printConnectDeprecation('vscode','--vscode') then connectTargets({targets:{vscode:true}})

business_review.item: §2 Three orthogonal target flags (--claude-desktop, --vscode, --vscode-claude-code) on connect
business_review.notes: all three .option() declarations added to the unified connect command

business_review.item: §2 Shared modifiers --profile/--force/--verbose/--insiders on connect
business_review.notes: all four options declared and threaded into ConnectOptions

business_review.item: §2/§3.3 --vscode-claude-code is a standalone target — no longer implies the Desktop config
business_review.notes: vscodeClaudeCode drives only runVscodeClaudeCode; it shares the claude-desktop daemon identity but writes no desktop config

business_review.item: §2 Bare connect target-list text matches the spec (flags, examples, help line)
business_review.notes: TARGET_LIST is byte-for-byte the spec block

business_review.item: §3.1 Single connectTargets orchestrator extracted to connect-orchestrator.ts; three thin wrappers delegate
business_review.notes: new module owns lifecycle; unified action + desktop/vscode aliases each build a target set and call connectTargets

business_review.item: §3.2 Single strict daemonMatchesRequest used for every invocation; loose desktop gate removed
business_review.notes: ensureDaemon uses daemonMatchesRequest for all callers; old telemetryMode!=='claude-desktop' gate deleted from index.ts

business_review.item: §3.3 Telemetry identity priority mapping (claude-desktop>vscode-claude-code>vscode-byok) onto two identities
business_review.notes: deriveDaemonIdentity: claudeDesktop||vscodeClaudeCode→claude-desktop, else vscode-byok; table matches; covered by parametrized tests

business_review.item: §3.3 No new telemetry value introduced
business_review.notes: spawnOptions is only {telemetryMode:'claude-desktop'} or {clientType:'vscode-byok'}; test asserts only the two existing identities

business_review.item: §3.4 Partial-failure exit/rollback semantics (any-fail→exit 1; all-fail+started→rollback; partial→keep daemon; startup fail→hard fail)
business_review.notes: anyFailed sets exitCode=1; allFailed&&startedInThisRun→rollbackDaemon; ensureDaemon throw caught→rollback if started+printProxyError; tests cover each

business_review.item: §3.4 After all requested targets run, print the per-target summary
business_review.notes: Resolved in check round (CR-002): printSummary(results) is now called unconditionally after dispatch; the results.length>1 gate was removed, so single-target success prints the 'Targets configured:' block. New unit test covers §3.4; proxy suite 141/141.

business_review.item: §3.5 Aliases print a highlighted (chalk bold/yellow) deprecation notice before doing work
business_review.notes: printConnectDeprecation uses chalk.bold.yellow and is called before connectTargets in both alias actions; text matches spec

business_review.item: §3.5 Aliases keep only originally-released modifiers, drop --vscode-claude-code, preserve vscode-byok surface
business_review.notes: desktop alias options reduced to --profile/--verbose/--force/--insiders (old --vscode-claude-code sub-flag removed); vscode alias unchanged→vscode-byok; wiring test asserts flag present on connect, absent on both aliases

business_review.item: §3.6 --insiders with no VS Code target warns and continues (does not error)
business_review.notes: insiders && !vscode && !vscodeClaudeCode prints exact 'Note: --insiders has no effect...' and proceeds; test confirms spawnDaemon still called

business_review.item: §5 Regression: vscode alias keeps `codemie proxy connect vscode` valid and clientType==='vscode-byok'
business_review.notes: vscode subcommand still registered; delegates to {vscode:true}→deriveDaemonIdentity vscode-byok, preserving the live-test surface

standards_review.notes: No commits in the review range — changes are working-tree scope (uncommitted). Commit-format is enforced later by commitlint/mr-creator.

eslint clean (0 warnings, zero-warning policy) and tsc --noEmit clean on the changed files. ES modules with .js import extensions, explicit return types on exports, interfaces for shapes, no `any`; secret-bearing logs still routed through sanitizeLogArgs.

gatewayKey/token still routed through sanitizeLogArgs in logs; no new secret logging introduced. The plaintext gatewayKey printed in the VS Code BYOK setup instructions is pre-existing (unchanged from the prior code) and intentional for user setup, not a regression. verifySsoCredentials unchanged; no injection or unsafe file/process handling added.

finding_status.notes: Fixed in connect-orchestrator.ts connectTargets catch: an explicit `return;` was added immediately after `printProxyError(error, 'Failed to connect proxy');` (with a clarifying comment). Control can no longer fall through to the per-target dispatch with unassigned state/config, independent of process.exit behavior. Verified present in the fix-up diff; tsc --noEmit clean (no unreachable-code error), eslint clean.

Fixed in connect-orchestrator.ts: printSummary(results) is now called unconditionally after dispatch; the results.length > 1 || anyFailed gate was removed. A single-target success now prints the 'Targets configured:' summary block per spec §3.4. A new unit test 'single successful target still prints the per-target summary (spec §3.4)' asserts this; full proxy suite passes 141/141.
